records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:11 — Pagination behavior has no test coverage for exact multiples of the page size, allowing the current phantom extra page to ship unnoticed.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: `totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` in admin-group.js.es6. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), totalPages becomes 3 while only 2 pages exist, producing a phantom extra page. The finding correctly identifies this off-by-one edge case (missing tests aside, the underlying math defect is introduced by this diff).

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:38 — Overlapping member-page requests can resolve out of order and replace the current page with stale members and offset because responses are applied without request identity checks.
records.rationale: findMembers in the diff sets offset and issues an async ajax call, then unconditionally applies result.meta.offset/user_count/members in the .then callback. Next/previous actions set offset and call findMembers; rapid clicking can cause overlapping requests whose responses resolve out of order, and nothing in the diff (no request token/sequence check) prevents a stale response from overwriting the current page. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — Membership mutations resolve before their follow-up reload finishes, so a failed reload silently reports success and leaves stale UI state.
records.rationale: In group.js, removeMember and addMembers both do `.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` without returning the inner promise (addMembers even ends with a bare `})`). The returned promise therefore resolves before findMembers completes, so callers cannot catch reload failures and a failed reload is silently treated as success, leaving stale members in the UI. The mechanism is verifiable directly in the diff.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Adding members performs one user lookup plus membership work per unbounded comma-separated username, creating avoidable N+1 database load.
records.rationale: The diff's add_members action does `usernames.split(",").each do |username| User.find_by_username(username)...` — one DB query plus group.add per username, with no bound on the number of usernames. The mechanism is accurately described and specific to newly added code (the controller action and the /members.json PUT route are both introduced in this diff). It is not a correctness defect, so it is a substantive non-bug performance/scalability concern, though the admin-only context limits its severity.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint accepts an uncapped limit, allowing authorized visitors to force arbitrarily large database reads and JSON serialization.
records.rationale: Verified from the diff: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in groups_controller#members has no upper bound, so any authorized visitor can request an unbounded member list, causing large DB reads and JSON serialization. The diff does introduce this client-controlled limit (previously non-automatic groups returned all members). It is a genuine resource-exhaustion/hardening concern for a new pagination surface, though not a clear correctness defect, so it fits important_non_bug: a specific, material review point grounded in cited diff code (a maintainer would plausibly add a max cap, e.g. 100)

records.rationale: The diff replaces the old automatic-group-only, default-200 pagination with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` on the public members endpoint, with no maximum cap. A client can pass limit=1000000 and force serialization of an arbitrarily large membership set; the previous code capped at 200 by default. This is a verifiable, diff-introduced resource-exhaustion/security weakness on a public route.
